b: The World Championship match is taking place from 24 November to 12 December and consists of a maximum of 14 classical games. The first player to score 7½ points wins the match and the world title. A rest day follows every three games. Sindarov has the white pieces in game one, with the players alternating colours thereafter.

The time control is 120 minutes for the first 40 moves and 30 minutes for the remainder of the game, with a 30-second increment per move from move 41. The players are not allowed to agree to a draw before Black's 40th move.
Should the match end in a 7–7 tie, the following tiebreaks will be played:
Four rapid games with a time control of 15 minutes plus 10-second increments.
Two rapid games with a time control of 10 minutes plus 5-second increments.
Two blitz games with a time control of 3 minutes plus 2-second increments.
Individual blitz games with the same time control (3+2), alternating colours until a decisive result is obtained.
The total prize fund amounts to US$2.5 million.
